correctness.rationale: For any nondegenerate triangle all sides are strictly shorter than semiperimeter s, hence a perimeter-halving pair cannot be contained in one edge. Choose the one of its two length-s arcs passing through the common vertex V of the endpoint edges (including vertex endpoint boundary cases). With distances u,v≥0 and u+v=s, law of cosines yields |pq|²=s²sin²(θ_V/2)+(u−v)²cos²(θ_V/2). This is ≥s²sin²(α/2). At a minimum-angle vertex the incident sides b,c exceed s/2 by c<a+b and a≤b≤c, so the two half-s arc points are feasible and attain equality. Positivity of cos(θ/2) and strict monotonicity of sin on (0,π/2) classify every minimizer; number is 1/2/3 depending on number of minimum-angle vertices. Heron and sin²(α/2)=yz/((x+y)(x+z)) for ordered tangents x=s−a≥y=s−b≥z=s−c>0 give A/h²=((x+y)(x+z)/s²)*sqrt(sx/(yz)). Here sx/(yz)≥3 and (x+y)(x+z)/s²≥4/9 (the latter from y≤(s−z)/2, z≤s/3), with simultaneous equality only x=y=z. Independent 3654 exact-rational ordered tangent triples and 505 direct piecewise boundary minimizations support but do not replace the continuum proof.
risks: Finite independent tests do not by themselves prove an infinite-domain theorem; analytic derivation supplies the universal bounds.
Degenerate triangles are outside domain; no limit-case equality with zero area is asserted.

value.rationale: Area relative to minimum perimeter-halving chord squared is explicitly motivated by the primary convex-geometry question. The known equilateral ratio and weaker general convex-cycle bound leave an exact natural geometric extremal subcase for arbitrary triangles. Elementary proof length does not negate its value; no general convex-cycle solution is claimed.
risks: The quantitative gain is class-specific and the proof relies on elementary laws; no implication for all convex cycles is established.
